Rashi on Gittin 35b:10:1.hebrew: משום איסורא - שמא על דבר איסור נדרה, כגון על גיבוי כתובה, וכגון "יאסרו עלי כל פירות שבעולם אם אעבור עבירה פלוני", ובא להתיר את נדרו סתם, ורוצה לעבור העבירה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:10:1.english: Because of a prohibition - Perhaps she vowed concerning a prohibited matter, such as regarding the collection of [her] ketubah, or such as [one who says], "May all fruits in the world be forbidden to me if I commit such-and-such a transgression," and he comes to have his vow dissolved without specifying [the details], and [in fact] wants to commit the transgression:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:1.hebrew: הנושא נשים בעבירה - כהן הנושא נשים פסולות לכהונה, פסול לעבודה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:1.english: One who marries women in transgression - A priest who marries women unfit for the priesthood is disqualified from the [Temple] service:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:2.hebrew: עד שידור הנאה - ממנה לגרשה, ומשנה היא בבכורות (דף מה:):
Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:2.english: Until he takes a vow [not to derive] benefit - from her [in order] to divorce her; and it is a Mishnah in Bekhorot (45b):

Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:3.english: He takes a vow - [not to derive] benefit:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:4.hebrew: ועובד - עבודה, ואע"פ שעדיין לא גרשה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:4.english: And serves - [performs the Temple] service, even though he has not yet divorced her:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:5.hebrew: יורד - מן העבודה לאחר שסיים, ומגרשה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:11:5.english: He descends - from the [Temple] service after he finishes, and divorces her:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:1:1.english: And we appraised them at five maneh - She brought them before us, and we appraised their value [at] five maneh:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:1:2.hebrew: גט יבמין הוה - יבמה היה זה שנתן לה גט לפוסלה על האחין, והיא באה לגבות כתובה מנכסי בעלה הראשון שנתארמלה הימנו:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:1:2.english: [That] was a levirate bill of divorce - This [man] was her brother-in-law who gave her a bill of divorce to disqualify her from [marrying] the [other] brothers, and she was coming to collect her marriage contract from the property of her first husband, from whom she had been widowed:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:2:1.english: They taught [this] only - that she collects [her ketubah] through her vow:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:2:2.english: [They taught this] only where she did not marry - to another [man] at the time of collecting [her] ketubah:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:3:1.hebrew: דמיפר לה בעל - והיא סומכת על כך, ונודרת וגובה על שקר:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:3:1.english: Because [her] husband nullifies [it] for her - And she relies on this, and takes a vow and collects falsely:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:3:2.english: With regard to prior [vows] - [Referring to] vows that preceded marriage:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:4:1.hebrew: צריך לפרט את הנדר - הנשאל לחכם על נדרו צריך לפרט היאך נדר הנדר הזה, וכי מפרטה קמיה דליתומים נדרה, וכך נדרה: "אם נהניתי מכתובתי כלום", לא שרו לה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:4:1.english: One must detail the vow - One who consults a sage regarding his vow must detail how he made this vow; and when she details before him that she vowed to the orphans, and thus she vowed: "If I have derived any benefit from my ketubah," they will not dissolve [it] for her:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:5:1.hebrew: ברבים - נודרת בפני עשרה, וקסבר נדר שהודר ברבים אין לו הפרה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:5:1.english: In public - She vows in the presence of ten [people], and [Rav Nachman] holds [that] a vow made in public cannot be nullified:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:6:1.hebrew: מאי לאו נדרה השתא - בשעת גבייה לאחר נשואין, וקשיא לרב הונא:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:6:1.english: What, is it not [that] she takes a vow now - at the time of collection, after marriage, and [thus] it is a difficulty for Rav Huna:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:6:2.hebrew: מעיקרא - נדרה קודם נשואין, גובה אף אחר נשואין, דאינו מיפר בקודמים, דכתיב: "ואם בית אישה נדרה" (במדבר ל׳:י״א):
Rashi on Gittin 35b:6:2.english: Initially - [If] she vowed before marriage, she collects [her marriage contract] even after marriage, because he [her husband] cannot annul prior [vows], as it is written: "And if she vowed in her husband's house" (Numbers 30:11):

Rashi on Gittin 35b:7:1.english: She takes a vow and collects - [This] implies [that] she takes a vow now:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:7:2.hebrew: תנאי היא - לקמן פליגי בה בפרקין (דף מה:), איכא למ"ד יש לו הפרה, ואליביה לא גביא, משום דמיפר לה:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:7:2.english: It is [a dispute between] Tannaim - They disagree about this later in our chapter (45b): there is one who says [a vow taken in public] has [the possibility of] nullification, and according to him she does not collect [her marriage contract after remarrying], because [her husband] can nullify [it] for her.

Rashi on Gittin 35b:7:3.hebrew: ואיכא למ"ד אין לו הפרה - ואליביה מדרינן לה ברבים וגביא:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:7:3.english: And there is one who says [a vow taken in public] does not have nullification - And according to him, we have her take a vow in public and she collects [her marriage contract].

Rashi on Gittin 35b:9:1.english: [That] he cuts short his statement - and [he] does not detail everything:

Rashi on Gittin 35b:9:2.hebrew: וחכם - אינו מיפר אלא לדעת מה שישמע, הילכך לא יפרט על מה נדר, אלא יאמר: כך נדרתי ואסרתי עלי פירות מין פלוני:
Rashi on Gittin 35b:9:2.english: And the sage - dissolves [the vow] only according to what he hears; therefore, he should not specify what he vowed about, rather he should say: "Thus I vowed, and I forbade upon myself fruits of such-and-such a kind":

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:11:1.hebrew: תנן הנושא נשים כו' - ה"ה דמצי למיפרך ממתניתין דהכא:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:11:1.english: We learned: One who marries women, etc. - The same applies, that [the Gemara] could have raised an objection from our Mishnah here:

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:11:2.hebrew: ותני עלה נודר ועובד יורש ומגרש - קשה לר"י, דאמאי הוצרך לאתויי "ותני עלה"? לפרוך ממתניתין גופיה, דקתני "פסול עד שידור הנאה", ואי אמרת אין צריך לפרט הנדר, ליחוש דלמא כו'! ונראה לי, דאמתניתין הוה מצי למימר דפסול מלעבוד אפי' גרשה, עד שידור הנאה שלא יקח לעולם נשים פסולות יותר. ולכך לא שייך למיפרך "ליחוש דלמא כו'", כיון דכבר גירש, תו ליכא למיחש דלמא ישאל על נדרו כדי ליקח נשים פסולות; אבל הא דתני "ועובד ומגרש", פריך שפיר: כיון דעדיין לא גרשה, יש לחוש דלמא אזל לגבי חכם ושרי ליה ולא יגרש:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:11:2.english: And it is taught with regard to this: He takes a vow and serves, he descends and divorces - It is difficult for the Ri: why did [the Gemara] need to bring "And it is taught with regard to this"? Let it raise the objection from the Mishnah itself, which teaches, "[He is] disqualified until he takes a vow [not to derive] benefit" — and if you say [that] he does not need to detail the vow, let us be concerned lest, etc.! And it seems to me that regarding the Mishnah, one could have said that he is disqualified from serving even if he has [already] divorced her, until he takes a vow [not to derive] benefit so that he will never again take disqualified women [as wives]. And therefore it is not appropriate to object, "let us be concerned lest, etc.," since he has already divorced [her], there is no longer [reason] to be concerned lest he request [dissolution] of his vow in order to take disqualified women [as wives]; however, [from] that which it teaches, "and serves, and divorces," [the Gemara] objects well: since he has not yet divorced her, there is [reason] to be concerned lest he go to a sage and [the sage] dissolve [it] for him, and he will not divorce [her]:

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:1:1.hebrew: גט יבמין הוה - פי' בקונטרס שנתן לה גט לפוסלה על האחין, וכתובתה על נכסי בעלה הראשון. וקשה, דלא היה להם להזכיר גט, דלא ניתנה כתובה ליגבות עד שתחלוץ, והיה להם לכתוב שחלצה. ואמר ר"י: גט יבמין הוה, דלאחר שנתייבמה גרשה היבם, וכתובתה על נכסי בעלה הראשון, ומוריא היתירא משום דקא טרחה קמי אחיו:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:1:1.english: It was a levirate bill of divorce - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres that [the brother-in-law] gave her a bill of divorce to disqualify her from [marrying] the [other] brothers, and her marriage contract [is collected] from the property of her first husband. And this is difficult, for [the court] should not have mentioned a bill of divorce, since a marriage contract is not given to be collected until she performs chalitzah, and they should have written that she performed chalitzah. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak said: "It was a levirate bill of divorce" [means] that after she was taken in levirate marriage, the brother-in-law divorced her, and her marriage contract [is collected] from the property of her first husband, and she rationalizes leniency [with respect to her vow] because she exerted herself before his brother:

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:2:1.hebrew: אבל נשאת אין מדירין אותה - וא"ת: וידורוה שלא תאכל ככר זה אם נהנית משל בעלה, ותאכל לאלתר בפנינו! וכן קשה בסמוך, דפריך "וליחוש דלמא אזלה לגבי חכם ושרי לה". ולרבי אליעזר דאמר בפרק נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף עה. ודף עו.) שיכול להפר כל נדרים שעתידה לידור, אתי שפיר, דאיכא למיחש שמא כבר הפר לה כל מה שעתידה לידור; אבל לשאר תנאי קשה! וי"ל שאינה חוששת אלא בנדר שעל ידה היא עומדת באיסור כל ימיה. וא"ת: ונדירה בפני בעלה, ויאמר לה "קיים ליכי", דאז אין יכול להפר, כדאמר בפ' נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף עט.)? וי"ל דחיישינן שמא יפר לה בלחש קודם שיאמר "קיים ליכי". וא"ת: וידירוה על דעת רבים, דאין לו הפרה, כדאמר אמימר לקמן? וי"ל דלענין נדרי אשתו אין לחלק בין ברבים בין על דעת רבים, וכיון דלרב הונא ברבים יש לה הפרה, ה"ה על דעת רבים; דכיון שאינה תלויה בדעתה, דיכול להפר אפילו בלא חרטה, כך יכול להפר בלא דעת רבים. וכי פריך "ודלמא אזלה לגבי חכם ושרי לה", הוה מצי לשנויי דמדרינן לה על דעת רבים, אלא דבלאו הכי משני שפיר. ועי"ל דרב הונא לית ליה דאמימר; והא דאמר אמימר אפי' למאן דאמר יש לו הפרה, לא קאי ארב הונא, אלא אדרבנן דרבי יהודה דמתניתין, דתנן (לקמן גיטין דף מה:): ר' יהודה אומר, כל נדר שידעו בו רבים לא יחזיר, משום פריצותא, שנדרה נדר שאין לו הפרה, ושלא ידעו בו רבים יחזיר, דלא חייש לקלקולא; ורבנן פליגי ואמרי לא יחזיר, משום קלקולא, ולא מפלגי בין ידעו רבים ללא ידעו בו רבים, אלמא יש לו הפרה. וכן משמע התם, דקאמר לרבנן: אטו התם מי חייל עלייהו שבועה כלל? משמע דלרבנן יש לו הפרה. וא"ת: לאמימר, והא על דעת רבים אין לו הפרה, א"כ ע"כ לא בכל ענין אמרי רבנן דלא יחזיר, דבעל דעת רבים ליכא קלקולא; א"כ, ברבים נמי מנא ליה דסברי דיש לו הפרה? וי"ל דברבים שהזכיר רבי יהודה, אם איתא דלרבנן אין לו הפרה, הוו להו לרבנן לפרושי ולחלק ולומר איפכא מדר' יהודה; אבל בעל דעת רבים אין לחוש, דלא איירי בה רבנן, דר' יהודה נמי לא הזכיר על דעת רבים. ועוד, דבעל דעת רבים לא פסיקא להו לרבנן למתני דיחזיר, דלפעמים יש היתר בעל דעת רבים, כגון מדעתם של אותם רבים או לדבר מצוה, ואיכא קלקולא; אבל ברבים, אם איתא דאין לו הפרה, הוי להו למתני דיחזיר, דמילתא דפסיקא היא, דבשום ענין אין לו הפרה, למ"ד אין לו הפרה, לא שנא לדבר מצוה ולא שנא לדבר הרשות, תדע דמעשה גבעונים לדבר מצוה היה:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:2:1.english: However, if she married, they do not administer a vow to her - And if you say: Let them administer a vow to her that she shall not eat this loaf if she has benefited from her [deceased] husband's [property], and let her eat [it] immediately before us! And similarly, it is difficult just below, where [the Gemara] asks: "But let us be concerned that perhaps she will go to a sage and he will dissolve [the vow] for her." Now, according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMe'orasah (Nedarim 75a and 76a) that [a husband] can nullify all vows that she will take in the future, it works out well, for there is reason to be concerned that perhaps he has already nullified for her all that she will take in the future; however, according to the other Tannaim, it is difficult! And one can answer that she is only concerned about a vow through which she remains under a prohibition all her days. And if you say: Let us administer the vow to her in the presence of her husband, and let him say to her, "It is upheld for you," for then he cannot nullify [it], as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMe'orasah (Nedarim 79a)? And one can answer that we are concerned that perhaps he will nullify [it] for her in a whisper before he says, "It is upheld for you." And if you say: Let them administer a vow to her on the basis of the public's consensus, which cannot be dissolved, as Ameimar says below? And one can answer that regarding his wife's vows, one does not distinguish between [a vow taken] in public and [one taken] on the basis of the public's consensus; and since according to Rav Huna, [a vow taken] in public can be nullified for her, the same applies [to one taken] on the basis of the public's consensus — for since it does not depend on her mind, as he can nullify [it] even without regret [on her part], so too he can nullify [it] without the public's consensus. And when [the Gemara] asks, "But perhaps she will go to a sage and he will dissolve [it] for her," it could have answered that we administer the vow to her on the basis of the public's consensus, except that even without that it answers well. And furthermore, one can answer that Rav Huna does not hold [the view] of Ameimar; and that which Ameimar said, "even according to the one who says it can be dissolved," does not refer to Rav Huna, but rather to the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Yehudah in the Mishnah, as we learned in a Mishnah (below, Gittin 45b): Rabbi Yehudah says: Any vow that the public knew about, he may not take [her] back, because of licentiousness, since she took a vow that cannot be dissolved; and [one] that the public did not know about, he may take [her] back, because he is not concerned about a ruinous outcome. And the Rabbis disagree and say: He may not take [her] back, because of a ruinous outcome, and they do not distinguish between [a case where] the public knew and [a case where] the public did not know — evidently it can be dissolved. And so too it is implied there, where [the Gemara] says regarding the Rabbis: "Is it really so that an oath takes effect upon them there at all?" — implying that according to the Rabbis it can be dissolved. And if you say: According to Ameimar, surely [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus cannot be dissolved; if so, perforce the Rabbis did not say in every case that he may not take [her] back, since in [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus there is no ruinous outcome; if so, regarding [a vow taken] in public as well, how does he know that they hold it can be dissolved? And one can answer that regarding [a vow taken] in public, which Rabbi Yehudah mentioned, if it were so that according to the Rabbis it cannot be dissolved, the Rabbis should have specified and distinguished and stated the opposite of Rabbi Yehudah; however, regarding [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus there is no need to be concerned, because the Rabbis were not speaking about it, as Rabbi Yehudah too did not mention [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus. And furthermore, regarding [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus, it is not categorical for the Rabbis to teach that he may take [her] back, because sometimes there is dissolution for [a vow taken] on the basis of the public's consensus, such as with the consent of that public or for the sake of a mitzvah, and there is a ruinous outcome; however, regarding [a vow taken] in public, if it were so that it cannot be dissolved, they should have taught that he may take [her] back, since it is a categorical matter, as under no circumstances can it be dissolved according to the one who says it cannot be dissolved — whether for the sake of a mitzvah or for a discretionary matter; know [this] from the fact that the incident of the Gibeonites was for the sake of a mitzvah:

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:4:1.hebrew: ליחוש דלמא אזלה לגבי חכם ושרי לה - משמע דאדרב הונא פריך, אבל אי לאו דרב הונא, לא הוה קשיא ליה אמתני'. ולמאי דפרישית דרב הונא פליג אאמימר, אתי שפיר, דאמתני' ליכא למיפרך, דהא איכא למימר דמדרינן לה על דעת רבים, אבל לרב הונא לא מצי לשנויי הכי. אבל למאי דפי' דגבי חכם מודה רב הונא דאין לו הפרה, בלא רב הונא הוה מצי למיפרך אמתני'! וי"ל דלא מצי למיפרך אמתני' בלא רב הונא, דאיכא למימר שנדיר אותה על זה הככר ותאכל לאלתר בפנינו; אבל לרב הונא, דקאמר ניסת אין מדירין אותה, ואין מועיל להדירה על הככר שאינה חוששת כיון דאינה באיסור כל ימיה, כי לא ניסת נמי ניחוש דלמא אזלה לגבי חכם ושרי לה. וא"ת: בין חכם בין בעל, איך יכולין להפר שלא בפני היתומים? הא אמרי' בנדרים בפ' ר"א (נדרים דף סה.) דהמודר הנאה מחבירו אין מתירין לו אלא בפניו, ויליף ממשה וצדקיהו: "במדין נדרת, במדין לך והתיר נדרך"! וי"ל דבדיעבד אם הפר מופר; תדע, מדסמיך צדקיהו, שהיה חסיד גמור, על מה שהתירו לו סנהדרין שלא בפני נבוכדנצר. ועוד, דטעם דאין מתירין לו אלא בפניו מפרש בירושלמי דנדרים, דאמר התם בפ' השותפין: המודר הנאה מחבירו בפניו — אין נשאל אלא בפניו, שלא בפניו — נשאל בין בפניו בין שלא בפניו; ר' יוחנן אמר: מפני הבושה, ור' יהושע בן לוי אמר: מפני החשד; ואתא הדא פלוגתא כהלין פלוגתא, דתניא: יום הכפורים צריך לפרט את מעשיו, דברי ר' יהודה בן בתירא, ר"ע אומר: אין צריך לפרט את מעשיו. פי': מפני הבושה — שנתבייש לפניו במה שנדר הנאה ממנו, וכן מפרט מעשיו כדי שיתבייש מחטאיו. ומ"ד מפני החשד, פי' שלא יחשדוהו שעבר על נדרו, ולכך נמי לא יפרט מעשיו שלא יחשדוהו בשאר עבירות. והשתא ניחא הכא, דלא שייך לא בושה ולא חשד, דלא ידעי אם קבלה כלום מכתובתה; והא דיליף ממשה וצדקיהו, היינו כר' יהושע בן לוי, דהתם מפני החשד איכא, מפני בושה ליכא:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:4:1.english: Let us be concerned that perhaps she will go to a sage and he will dissolve [the vow] for her - This implies that [the Gemara] is challenging Rav Huna, whereas were it not for Rav Huna, it would not have had a difficulty with the Mishnah. According to what I explained [above], that Rav Huna disagrees with Ameimar, this works out well, for on the Mishnah one cannot raise a difficulty, since one could say that we administer the vow to her on the condition of public consent (al da'at rabbim), whereas according to Rav Huna one cannot answer thus. However, according to what I explained [above], that with respect to a sage Rav Huna agrees that it has no dissolution, [then] even without Rav Huna one could have raised a difficulty with the Mishnah! And one can say that one could not raise a difficulty with the Mishnah without Rav Huna, because one could say that we administer a vow to her regarding this loaf [of bread] and she eats [it] immediately before us; whereas according to Rav Huna, who says [that once] she has married we do not administer a vow to her, and administering a vow to her regarding the loaf is of no avail because she is not concerned [about a vow] since she is not in a state of prohibition all her days — when she has not married as well, let us be concerned that perhaps she will go to a sage and he will dissolve [the vow] for her! And if you ask: Whether a sage or a husband, how can they annul [the vow] not in the presence of the orphans? Surely we say in Nedarim, in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer (Nedarim 65a), that one who is prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from his fellow may only have it dissolved in his presence, and [the Gemara] derives this from Moses and Zedekiah: "In Midian you vowed; in Midian go and dissolve your vow"! And one can say that after the fact, if he annulled [it], it is annulled; know [that this is so] from the fact that Zedekiah, who was completely pious, relied upon what the Sanhedrin dissolved for him not in the presence of Nebuchadnezzar. Furthermore, the reason that one may only dissolve [it] for him in his presence is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud on Nedarim, where it says there in the chapter [entitled] Hashutafin: One who is prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from his fellow in his presence may only request [dissolution] in his presence; [if he vowed] not in his presence, he may request [dissolution] either in his presence or not in his presence. Rabbi Yochanan said: Because of shame; and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Because of suspicion. And this dispute parallels that [other] dispute, as it was taught [in a baraita]: [On] Yom Kippur one must specify his deeds, [these are] the words of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira; Rabbi Akiva says: One need not specify his deeds. Meaning: [according to the one who says] "because of shame" — that he should feel ashamed before him regarding that which he vowed [not to derive] benefit from him, and similarly he specifies his deeds so that he will feel ashamed of his sins. And the one who says "because of suspicion" — meaning, so that they should not suspect him of having transgressed his vow; and therefore also he should not specify his deeds, so that they should not suspect him of other transgressions. Now it works out well here, for neither shame nor suspicion applies, since they do not know whether she received anything from her marriage contract. And that which [the Gemara] derives from Moses and Zedekiah accords with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, for there suspicion applies, [whereas] shame does not apply:

Tosafot on Gittin 35b:4:2.hebrew: קסבר צריך לפרט את הנדר - בירושלמי משמע דהכי קיימא לן, דההוא דאתא קמיה דר' בון, אמר ליה: התיר לי נדרי. אמר ליה: מאי נדרת? א"ל: נדרית דלא מרווחנא. אמר ליה: וכי עבדין כדין? אמר ליה: לצחק בקוביא קאמינא. אמר ליה: ברוך שבחר בדברי חכמים, שאמרו צריך לפרט את הנדר, דאי לאו דפרטת לנדר, התרתיהו לך. וא"ת: בפ' שום היתומין (ערכין דף כג) גבי מקדיש נכסיו והי' עליו כתובה (ובעל חוב), דקאמר ר' אליעזר כשהוא מגרשה ידור הנאה, ור' יהושע אומר אינו צריך, ומפרש דפליגי בנדר שהודר ברבים, דרבי אליעזר סבר דאין לו הפרה, ור' יהושע סבר יש לו הפרה, ו"אינו צריך" דקאמר היינו דאינו מועיל; וא"כ, תקשי כדפריך התם לעיל: לימא רב הונא כתנאי אמר לשמעתיה, דכיון דרב הונא סבר צריך לפרט, אמאי אינו מועיל? וא"כ הא דרב הונא דצריך לפרט הויא כתנאי! ומיהו לא קיימא התם מסקנא הכי:
Tosafot on Gittin 35b:4:2.english: He holds that one must detail the vow - In the Yerushalmi it is implied that we hold thus [in practice]: for a certain man came before R' Bun [and] said to him, "Dissolve my vow for me." [R' Bun] said to him, "What did you vow?" He said to him, "I vowed that I would not profit." [R' Bun] said to him, "Do people do such a thing?!" He said to him, "I meant [profiting] by playing dice." [R' Bun] said to him, "Blessed is He who chose the words of the Sages, who said that one must detail the vow; for had you not detailed the vow, I would have dissolved it for you!" And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Shum HaYetomin (Arakhin 23a), regarding one who consecrates his property and had a ketubah [obligation] (and a creditor) upon him, where R' Eliezer says: "When he divorces her, he must vow [not to derive] benefit [from her]," and R' Yehoshua says: "He does not need to," and [the Gemara] explains that they disagree regarding a vow that was vowed in public — for R' Eliezer holds that it has no dissolution, whereas R' Yehoshua holds that it has dissolution, and "he does not need to" that he says means that it is of no avail — and if so, it should be difficult, just as [the Gemara] asks there earlier: "Shall we say that Rav Huna stated his teaching in accordance with [a dispute of] Tannaim?" For since Rav Huna holds that one must detail [the vow], why is it of no avail [according to R' Yehoshua]? And if so, this [ruling] of Rav Huna, that one must detail [the vow], would be [a matter of dispute between] Tannaim! However, the conclusion there [in Arakhin] does not stand like this:
